passage: In the colony lane, Rekha, two, pointed sharply at something over the gate. Her mother Simran assumed it was the ice-cream cart. “You want ice cream?” Rekha shook her head and pointed again, harder. Simran crouched to Rekha's height and followed her eyes, and there behind the gate sat a small brown dog. “Oh, a doggy!” Rekha laughed and pointed again. “Dog,” said Simran, and this time Rekha repeated, “Da!”

qa.q: What did Simran first think Rekha was pointing at?
qa.a: The ice-cream cart.

qa.q: What was Rekha trying to share, and what showed it?
qa.a: She wanted Simran to look at the dog, and her shaking head, harder point and laugh showed it. She might also have wanted to say the dog was interesting or a little scary.

qa.q: What could Simran do next time Rekha points?
qa.a: She could check where Rekha is looking before guessing, as she did this time, and name what she sees.

qa.q: How might Simran feel when Rekha shakes her head at the ice-cream guess?
qa.a: Simran may feel a little puzzled at first, and then pleased when she crouches, follows Rekha's eyes and finds the dog.

grounding: A toddler points to direct attention, and the caregiver checks what the child is really looking at before guessing.

passage:
“Neelam, look, a dog!” said Swati, pointing across the park.
Neelam turned her head and looked. “Dog.”
“That's right. He's brown.”
A minute later Neelam pointed at the kitchen cupboard when they got home.
“Biscuit?” said Swati.
Neelam shook her head.
“Cup? Juice?”
Neelam kept pointing until Swati looked closer and saw the toy dog on the shelf below.
“The toy dog! Of course.”
Neelam grinned.

qa.q: What did Neelam actually want from the cupboard area?
qa.a: The toy dog on the shelf below.

qa.q: What did Neelam feel when Swati kept guessing food?
qa.a: She probably felt a bit frustrated that her point was not understood, and pleased when Swati looked closer. She may also just have been excited to share her interest in dogs.

qa.q: How could Swati make guessing easier?
qa.a: Swati could follow Neelam's eyes and finger first, then ask a question, and say the name of what she finds.

qa.q: What might Swati feel when she finally sees the toy?
qa.a: Swati may feel amused and a little sorry for jumping to conclusions, glad the mystery is solved. 🙂

grounding: A toddler follows an adult's point and points to share interest, and the caregiver checks what the child looks at before guessing.

passage: Daycare note, Wednesday. Tenzin pointed up toward the shelf and said, "Da!" I handed him the ball. He shook his head and kept pointing. I tried the blocks. Another shake. Then I followed his eyes instead of his finger. He was looking past the shelf, at a small bird on the window ledge. "Bird!" I said. He smiled wide and pointed again. Next time I will check where he is looking first. Ganga, daycare teacher

qa.q: What was Tenzin actually looking at?
qa.a: A small bird on the window ledge, past the shelf.

qa.q: What was Tenzin likely feeling when he kept pointing after getting the ball?
qa.a: He was probably frustrated at not being understood, and delighted once Ganga named the bird, as his wide smile shows.

qa.q: What did Ganga learn to do next time?
qa.a: To follow Tenzin's eyes and check what he is looking at before guessing what his pointing means.

qa.q: What was it like for Tenzin when Ganga kept handing him the wrong things?
qa.a: It was likely confusing and a little frustrating, since he wanted to share the bird, not get a toy.

grounding: A teacher learns to check what a toddler is actually looking at before guessing what his pointing means.

passage:
In the village lane in Goa, Farhan from next door crouched beside Elizabeth and pointed. "Look, a goat!" Elizabeth followed his finger and stared at the goat chewing a leaf.
Later, under the mango tree, she pointed up and grunted. Farhan reached for a low mango. "This one?"
She shook her head, still pointing. Farhan looked where her eyes were. A squirrel was running along the branch. "Oh! Squirrel!" Elizabeth grinned and bounced.

qa.q: What was the goat doing?
qa.a: Chewing a leaf.

qa.q: Why did Elizabeth shake her head when Farhan reached for the mango?
qa.a: She felt misunderstood, because she wasn't asking for the mango; she wanted to share the squirrel, and she was delighted once he saw it.

qa.q: What could Farhan do first next time Elizabeth points?
qa.a: Check where her eyes are looking before guessing, since a point can mean "look at this" as well as "I want that".

qa.q: How might Farhan feel when Elizabeth bounces with a grin?
qa.a: He likely feels pleased and a bit amused that he finally found what she meant.

grounding: A toddler follows a neighbour's point and then points to share interest, and he learns to check what she is looking at.

passage:
Outside a bakery in Kyoto, Kaito pulled on Lucia's hand and pointed hard at the window. "Ah! Ah!"
"You want bread? We have bread at home," said Lucia.
Kaito pointed harder, stamping. Lucia bent down to his level and looked along his arm. Behind the bread, a grey cat lay curled on a chair. "A cat! Sleeping!" Kaito's stamping stopped. He pressed his nose to the glass, smiling.

qa.q: Where was the cat lying?
qa.a: Curled on a chair behind the bread.

qa.q: What was Kaito feeling when he pointed harder and stamped?
qa.a: He was frustrated that Lucia guessed he wanted bread; once she saw the cat, he felt understood and happy.

qa.q: What went wrong at first, and what fixed it?
qa.a: Lucia guessed the point meant "I want that"; bending down to look along his arm showed he meant "look at this", and fixed it.

qa.q: How might Lucia see the moment afterwards?
qa.a: She may feel a little sheepish about guessing bread, and glad she took a closer look.

grounding: A carer checks what a toddler is actually looking at and learns his point meant "look" rather than "I want".

passage:
I'm Farhan. My baby brother Hrithik is learning to point.
Last week Abbu pointed at a dog outside the shop. Hrithik looked at his finger first, then followed it to the dog and gasped.
Yesterday Hrithik pointed at the shelf and went “Uh! Uh!” I thought he wanted his ball and handed it to him. He pushed it away and pointed again.
I crouched down to his height. He wasn't looking at the ball. He was looking at the cat on top of the shelf.

qa.q: What did Abbu point at outside the shop?
qa.a: Abbu pointed at a dog outside the shop.

qa.q: What was Hrithik feeling when he pushed the ball away and pointed again?
qa.a: He was frustrated that Farhan had misunderstood him, and still eager to share his interest in the cat.

qa.q: What did Farhan learn to do before guessing what Hrithik wants?
qa.a: Farhan got down to Hrithik's height to see what he was actually looking at, which showed the point meant the cat, not the ball.

qa.q: What would change if Farhan had kept handing Hrithik toys without looking?
qa.a: Hrithik would likely get more upset and learn that his pointing is not understood, and the cat would never be shared.

grounding: It illustrates a toddler following an adult's point and starting to point himself, and a caregiver checking what he actually looks at before guessing.
